The screens nobody drew, listed before anyone asks for them

/fig:prep reads what each screen contains and works out which states it must also have. What it cannot find, it stubs as a dashed placeholder — so the gap sits on the canvas instead of in someone's head.
After prepRow one was drawn. Row two is what nobody drew yet.
Solid frames are real screens. Each dashed one carries the state it stands for and why it is there, and stays dashed until someone draws it — so a glance at the page tells you how much is left.
/fig:prep — 3 screens read · 5 states stubbed
list_emptya list has to say something when it holds nothing
list_loadingit fetches, so there is a moment before it has anything
detail_errorthe fetch can fail, and the screen still has to render
edit_invalidthe form validates, so it can reject
edit_savingthe save is not instant
This is why prep runs before the drawing, not after. The stub list is the to-draw list — and every one of these is a question engineering would otherwise ask halfway through the build.
